history.period: 18th century CE - built by Raja Umed Singh of Chamba; one vlog says 1754 CE, one Tripadvisor review says 1762 (conflict - verify exact year)
history.summary: The Chamunda Devi temple at Dev Kothi (also called Devi Kothi) is an 18th-century Shakti temple in Chamba district dedicated to Goddess Chamunda, the fierce Durga-form who slew the demons Chanda and Munda. Consulted sources agree it was built by Raja Umed Singh of Chamba (one source: 1754 CE after a fulfilled wish; a Tripadvisor review: 1762 - exact year unverified). The temple exemplifies Pahari/Himachali wooden architecture - carved wood, slate roof, wall paintings and murals in the Chamba miniature tradition depicting Chamunda's victory over the demons and Devi Mahatmya scenes (some Mughal/Vaishnavite influence noted). The Mindhal copperplate inscription (1641 CE) of Raja Prithvi Singh records a village donation to a Chamunda Devi temple, and the Chamba riyasat's goddess traditions trace Devi worship to the 7th-century Meru Varman; the temple was renovated over the centuries. IDENTITY FLAG: this entry documents the documented 18th-century Dev Kothi temple, but the geocoder matches a separate 'Chamunda Devi Temple' at Karman Main Road, Mohalla Sapri, Chamba town (32.55422, 76.12963), and the CSV detail hint mentions a 'Champavati temple precinct' connection that no consulted source confirms (verify which shrine the CSV row intends; do not conflate with the Chamunda Nandikeshwar temple near Dharamshala, Kangra district). CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name ('Chamba') - the real state is HIMACHAL PRADESH.

town_description: Chamba is the old princely-capital town of Chamba district, Himachal Pradesh, set on a plateau on the right bank of the Ravi at about 996 m, founded c. 920 CE by Raja Sahil Varman. It is a historic centre of Devi worship in the western Himalaya; the district also includes the 18th-century Devi Kothi Chamunda temple in the Churah valley.
